extraction.name: NWPU-RESISC45
extraction.description: NWPU-RESISC45 is a publicly available benchmark dataset for Remote Sensing Image Scene Classification (RESISC), created by Northwestern Polytechnical University (NWPU). It contains 31,500 images covering 45 scene classes with 700 images per class, with image sizes of 256×256 pixels in the RGB color space and spatial resolutions varying from about 30 m to 0.2 m per pixel.
extraction.creator: Gong Cheng, Junwei Han, Xiaoqiang Lu
extraction.citeAs: Gong Cheng, Junwei Han, and Xiaoqiang Lu, "Remote Sensing Image Scene Classification: Benchmark and State of the Art," Proceedings of the IEEE, 2016.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was extracted from Google Earth by experts in the field of remote sensing image interpretation. The 31,500 images cover more than 100 countries and regions across developing, transition, and highly developed economies, carefully chosen under all kinds of weathers, seasons, illumination conditions, imaging conditions, and scales.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Google Earth (Google Inc.), which maps the Earth via superimposition of images obtained from satellite imagery, aerial photography, and geographic information system (GIS) onto a 3D globe.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images were extracted with a fixed size of 256×256 pixels in the red green blue (RGB) color space, with spatial resolutions varying from about 30 m to 0.2 m per pixel.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Representative scene classes were selected by identifying 30 widely-used scene categories from existing datasets and an additional 15 categories by searching literature keywords on Web of Science and Google Scholar, totaling 45 classes. Images were then categorized and selected into these 45 classes (700 images per class) by experts in remote sensing image interpretation.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Experts in the field of remote sensing image interpretation.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The scene classes of island, lake, mountain, and snowberg have lower spatial resolutions compared to other classes. Additionally, remote sensing overhead imagery cannot capture the ground detail and vertical characteristics available in ground photos.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Remote sensing image scene classification, algorithm development, evaluation, and benchmarking (training and testing data-driven algorithms including handcrafted features, unsupervised feature learning, and deep learning models). Evaluated under 10%-90% and 20%-80% training-testing splits.
